The test image shows:
- Stem at/near the soil line with white cottony mycelium
- Small dark rounded sclerotia embedded in the white growth
- Stem rotting/collapsing at the base
- Plant appears wilted/dead above

This is strongly suggestive of Southern Blight (Sclerotium rolfsii) — white mycelium + small round sclerotia at the soil line is the hallmark. Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference confirms the context: Southern Blight causes tomato plant collapse with stem rot at soil level, on plastic mulch beds — matching the test image perfectly.

The test image shows:
- White cottony mycelium on stem at soil line (classic Sclerotium rolfsii sign)
- Small round dark sclerotia embedded in the mycelium
- Stem collapse/rot at soil level
- Black plastic mulch visible in background (same production context)

All features are diagnostic for Southern Blight.
